title: What Is a Symbolic Representation
content:
OBJECTIVE: Develop a rigorous understanding of what is a symbolic representation within foundational representation and information theory.

CORE IDEA: A symbolic representation maps source information into a defined alphabet or structured feature space. The mapping must be described precisely enough that another implementation can reproduce it. Compactness alone does not prove compression; preservation, reconstruction, collisions, and task performance must be measured.

WORKED APPLICATION: Define a source, choose a representation, specify the conversion rule, and list what information survives. Compare the representation with the original and record storage cost, ambiguity, and failure modes. If exact reconstruction is required, demonstrate byte-for-byte recovery; if the representation is intentionally lossy, define the semantic task it is intended to preserve.

PRACTICE: 1) State the input and output domains. 2) Write the conversion rule in plain language. 3) Identify information that is preserved and discarded. 4) Design one measurable test. 5) Explain one way the representation could collide or fail.

MASTERY STANDARD: You can distinguish encoding, compression, hashing, feature extraction, and semantic representation; calculate or estimate representation cost; and design an experiment that can falsify an unsupported compression claim.
